idiom_name: nil with the safe navigation operator &. and nil?-guarded defaults
implementation_notes: Ruby's absence value is nil, the single instance of NilClass, and it is what missing lookups return; absence travels in the signature only as documentation, because Ruby has no static types. The idiom that replaces a Maybe wrapper is the safe navigation operator: the official syntax reference defines &. as skipping the method call and returning nil when the receiver is nil, without evaluating the arguments - and it skips exactly one call, so every hop of a chain needs its own &. Hash#fetch with a default, Array#dig, nil? checks and the or/or= operators carry the rest. A monadic Maybe (dry-monads) exists for pipeline code where a series of computations may return nil at any point; it is a library choice rather than idiomatic Ruby.
code_sketch:
city = order&.customer&.address&.city || "unknown"

port = Integer(raw, exception: false)   # nil when not a valid integer
port ||= 8080                            # default at the call site
pitfalls: false and nil are both falsey but only nil is absence, 0 is truthy in Ruby while '' is not: ||, ||= and blank? all blur the distinction, so nil checks must be explicit where it matters.
&. skips one call only: order&.customer.address still raises NoMethodError when the customer is nil; every hop needs &. or a fetch/dig form that reports absence.
Nothing forces a caller to handle nil without RBS/Sorbet signatures; the missed case surfaces as NoMethodError on nil at run time.

variants.name: dry-monads Maybe
variants.implementation_notes: dry-monads provides the monadic realization: Maybe(user) wraps a possibly-nil value as Some or None, bind chains further nil-able steps, fmap maps wrapped values, and value_or is the documented safe way out (value! raises on None, to_result converts to a Result carrying a reason). The docs describe it as the tool for a series of computations that could return nil at any point, and note the deliberate difference from &. - it wraps rather than short-circuiting message sends. Choose it where pipelines of nil-able lookups dominate and the dry-rb stack is already a dependency.
variants.code_sketch:
extend Dry::Monads[:maybe]

maybe_street = Maybe(user).bind do |u|
  Maybe(u.address).bind do |a|
    Maybe(a.street)
  end
end

label = maybe_street.value_or("unknown")
pitfalls: Maybe(...) coerces nil to None while false stays a value; every call site has to decide whether false counts as absence.
In 1.x, fmap coerces a nil block result to None - the documentation says this changes in 2.0 because it violates the functor laws, so pipeline meaning can shift on upgrade.
The library adds a monad vocabulary next to plain nil handling; mixing both in one code base requires converting at the boundary and agreeing per layer.
